title: Legal Research Assistant with Citation Checking
summary: A research assistant that answers only from retrieved judgments and statutes, quotes the passage it relies on, and checks each citation for existence, accuracy and later treatment.

seo.title: Legal Research Assistant with Citation Checking | VipraTech
seo.description: A legal research assistant that grounds answers in retrieved judgments, verifies every citation and quote, and checks drafts for fabricated case law.

problem.intro: General-purpose chatbots produce fluent legal answers with citations that may not exist, misquote a judgment or ignore that it was later overruled. Courts in several jurisdictions have criticised filings that relied on such citations. Lawyers still need faster research, but only in a form they can verify before it goes into an opinion or a written submission.

pain_points.title: Fabricated or garbled citations
pain_points.detail: Party names, years, reporters and paragraph numbers can be invented or mixed up by unconstrained models.

pain_points.title: Good law or not
pain_points.detail: A judgment may have been overruled, distinguished or referred to a larger bench, and research notes rarely say so.

pain_points.title: New criminal laws
pain_points.detail: References to the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act now need mapping to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, BNSS and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, in force since July 2024.

pain_points.title: Drafts from many hands
pain_points.detail: Written submissions combine research from associates, interns and outside tools, and nobody checks every citation end to end.

solution.overview: We build a research assistant that retrieves from sources you are licensed to use and from your firm's own opinions and briefs, and answers only with propositions it can support from retrieved text. Each proposition carries its citation and the quoted paragraph. A separate citation checker then verifies that each case exists in the source, that the citation and paragraph number match, and that quoted text appears verbatim, and it flags available signals of later treatment and bench strength for the lawyer to check. The same checker runs on any draft, so citations from any source are verified before filing.
capabilities: Retrieval over licensed case-law databases and your internal knowledge bank
Answers built only from retrieved passages, with a quoted paragraph for each proposition
Citation existence, format and paragraph checks across law reports and neutral citations
Verbatim quote verification against the judgment text
Flags signals of later treatment and bench strength for lawyer review
Draft checker that verifies every citation in a brief, opinion or written submission

workflow.title: Pose the question
workflow.detail: The lawyer enters a research question with jurisdiction, forum and any key facts, or uploads a draft to check.

workflow.title: Retrieve sources
workflow.detail: Relevant judgments, statutes and internal opinions are retrieved from licensed and internal sources.

workflow.title: Draft a grounded answer
workflow.detail: A draft answer is built only from retrieved passages, each proposition with its citation and quote.

workflow.title: Verify citations
workflow.detail: Each citation is checked for existence, accuracy, quote match and treatment signals.

workflow.title: Handle failures
workflow.detail: Citations that fail any check are removed or clearly marked, never left silently in the answer.

workflow.title: Lawyer review
workflow.detail: The lawyer reads the cited paragraphs, checks treatment and decides what to rely on.

Internal opinions, briefs and research notes

human_in_the_loop: Lawyers read the cited paragraphs and decide what to rely on; the assistant never presents an answer as advice. Treatment signals are prompts to check, and the lawyer confirms whether a judgment is still good law.
integrations: Licensed legal research databases (via API or permitted access)
Document management system and knowledge bank
Microsoft Word add-in for draft checking
guardrails: No citation appears in an answer unless the judgment was retrieved from a source
Every quote verified verbatim against the judgment text
Unverified citations removed or visibly marked, never silently kept
Answers labelled as a research aid, not legal advice
Use of licensed content stays within licence terms
compliance_notes: Research queries can reveal client matters, so queries and logs stay within your environment under access control.
Use of licensed databases follows each publisher's licence terms.

pilot.scope: One practice area, such as arbitration or cheque dishonour matters, with the draft checker run on recent submissions and the assistant used on live research questions.
deliverables: Source connections and retrieval tuned for the practice area
Word add-in or upload checker for drafts

faqs.q: How is this different from a general chatbot?
faqs.a: It answers only from judgments and statutes it has actually retrieved, quotes the paragraph it relies on and runs a separate check on every citation. If a citation cannot be verified, it is removed or marked rather than presented as fact.

faqs.q: Can it tell us whether a case is still good law?
faqs.a: It flags signals of later treatment and bench strength from the sources available. The lawyer must check those signals and confirm the position before relying on the judgment.

faqs.q: Does it handle the new criminal laws?
faqs.a: Yes. It maps IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act references to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, BNSS and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam where a mapping exists, and flags where provisions differ.

faqs.q: Can it check drafts prepared outside the tool?
faqs.a: Yes. Upload a draft or use the Word add-in, and every citation and quotation is checked against the sources, whoever or whatever produced it.
